study_identification.title: Capturing the Individual Deviations From Normative Models of Brain Structure for Depression Diagnosis and Treatment

study_characteristics.study_objective: The study aimed to investigate the clinical issues related to depression according to individual deviations from normative ranges of gray matter volume. They developed a normative modeling approach to capture personalized deviations and guide clinical diagnosis and treatment of depression.

quality_checking_detail.answer: Participants with incomplete clinical data or poor imaging quality were also excluded.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: ComBat harmonization by site with covariates age, sex, and TIV.

software_tool.answer: PCNtoolkit; Python 3.6; MATLAB 2019b; SPM12; CAT12; LIBSVM

predictor_effects.answer: Age and sex are fixed effects. TIV is a nuisance covariate.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study used ComBat for harmonization to handle site effects and included TIV as a covariate to handle nuisance from total intracranial volume.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: To minimize the nonbiological variance introduced by differences in MRI scanners and acquisition protocols, we used the ComBat method (30) to harmonize data from these three datasets. ... we estimated an age-related normative model with datasets II and III (n = 510 + 229 = 739) (Figure 1B, top) to predict regional GMV as a function of age and sex plus nuisance covariate TIV using a B-spline Bayesian linear regression (37).
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.location: Shao2024.pdf.md, page 3, line 10 and page 4, line 1.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model performance was evaluated using cross-validation on the training data.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: In different splits of sample, the proportion of patients and HC participants remained consistent in both the training (102 patients vs. 88 HC participants) and the test (25 patients vs. 22 HC participants) sets. Moreover, feature selection was performed using max-relevance and minredundancy (41) with 10-fold cross-validation.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The model was validated on an independent test set from the same hospital.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Then, each trained model was used to predict the diagnostic category for each participant in the corresponding test set, which was rebuilt and tested during the 10,000 resampling procedure.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The model was validated on an external test set from a different hospital.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Finally, each model trained in the discovery cohort was applied to the external test set to evaluate the generalizability and transportability of the models under different sites (Figure 1C, left).

clinical_dataset.answer: Dataset I (Affiliated Brain Hospital of Nanjing Medical University and Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital)

clinical_groups_sex.answer: Discovery DP: F 61, M 66; External test DP: F 39, M 21

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Machine learning models (SVM) were trained to diagnose depressed patients using z-scores. A Bayesian model (polar Latent Dirichlet Allocation) was used to find latent brain factors in relation to antidepressant treatment.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Capturing personalized deviations from a normative range could help in understanding the heterogeneous neurobiology of depression and thus guide clinical diagnosis and treatment of depression.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The normative modeling approach revealed highly individualized patterns of anatomic abnormalities in depressed patients. Models trained with individual normative probability maps (AUC range, 0.7146–0.7836) showed better performance than models trained with original gray matter volume values (AUC range, 0.6800–0.7036). Different latent brain structural factors in relation to antidepressant treatment were revealed by a Bayesian model based on normative probability maps, suggesting distinct treatment response and inclination.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The normative age modeling was based on cross-sectional data and should be validated with longitudinal data. The study focused on patients between 18 and 65 years of age. More subtype samples can be added to the normative model.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study provides a framework for using normative models to guide clinical diagnosis and treatment of depression.

general_notes.general_notes: The study used a novel approach to analyze brain structure in depression, focusing on individual deviations from a normative model rather than group-level differences. This approach has the potential to be more clinically relevant.
